disclaimer: 21+ adults only. Educational geography and plant-type talk — not medical advice, not cultivation advice, not a live menu.

types.name: Indica
types.history: The word indica has been used for short, broad-leaf plants tied to highland Central Asia. Think resin-rich mountain populations and short seasons — culture and botany, not a dosing chart.
types.originNote: Classic pins sit on the Hindu Kush range and northern Afghanistan.

types.name: Sativa
types.history: Sativa, in shop talk, usually means taller, narrower-leaf expressions from warmer latitudes. Names like Thai, Durban, Colombian, Mexican, Jamaican, and Acapulco Gold are trade and landrace stories — not grow recipes.
types.originNote: Pins run from Southeast Asia to southern Africa, the Caribbean, and highland Mexico.

types.name: Hybrid
types.history: Most modern shop flower is a hybrid of older regional lines. The Indian subcontinent, for example, holds a long cultural record that spans fiber, ritual, and mixed highland expressions — a reminder that types blur at the edges.
types.originNote: See hybrid-landrace pins on the Origins map — educational geography only.

types.name: Hemp
types.history: Hemp is the fiber-and-seed side of the cannabis story. East Asia — especially the Yellow River basin — has deep archaeological and historical records of hemp for cloth, seed, and ceremony.
types.originNote: Not a high-THC shop type. History of use, not a grow guide.

types.name: Ruderalis
types.history: C. ruderalis is tied to short-season northern latitudes — roadside and steppe habitats across southern Russia and east-central Europe. Breeders later borrowed the day-neutral habit. We talk history, not how to breed.
types.originNote: The Origins map marks the ruderalis belt as geography, not a product list.
